title: a dynamic asset import whose specifier is not a literal is rejected: a loader that cannot be selected at compile time cannot be selected at all
notes: This is the sharpest statement of static loader selection there is: `chosen` is a `const` initialized one line earlier to the literal the program would have been allowed to write inline, so a reader can see that the refusal is about WHEN the specifier is known to the compiler rather than about what it says. Constant-folding it would be the wrong fix — the rule is that the specifier is a literal at the import, because the alternative is a compiler that resolves assets by evaluating arbitrary expressions. The declared position 4:24 is the `import(` call, not `chosen`: poc/src/build/source-assets.ts:357-366 reports the deferred site on the node it could not read statically. `config.json` IS staged, so the case cannot pass for want of a file. Everything after the refusal is unreachable on the reference, which is why `loaded.default.mode` never has to type-check. The rule is docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked): 'Every non-code or foreign-source import uses standard import attributes. The required string-valued `type` selects its loader', and 'Loading happens during compilation. It does not add `FileSystem` or another runtime platform requirement to the importing program.' The same page names this spelling on the unsupported side: 'nonliteral dynamic imports/attributes ... remain unsupported.' RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to ACCEPT this program and emit a RUNTIME dynamic import of the asset — zero diagnostics where the reference reports SMITHERS5218@4:24, `emitSkipped: false`, and the emitted JavaScript executed by node exited 1 with `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '<out>/config.json' imported from '<out>/a-non-literal-dynamic-asset-import-is-rejected.js'`. That stack trace was the evidence and it was stronger than a missing diagnostic: the file was not missing from the project, it was missing from the OUTPUT, because the fork compiled a compile-time asset load into a runtime filesystem read — the fail-open direction of both Locked sentences above at once. The fork already owned the neighbouring static rules (SMITHERS5201-5209, 5213, 5215-5217), so it was the DYNAMIC spelling specifically that was unowned. It closed it by routing literal dynamic asset sites through the same loader/admission pipeline as a static asset edge and refusing computed specifiers and computed attribute objects before emit (compiler/forkbridge/assets.go.txt, lowering.go.txt); the same change also made a literal dynamic asset import compile and embed rather than report TS2307, and gave a literal asset dynamic import with no attributes its proper SMITHERS5201. Measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`, and re-measured before retirement by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend go --filter a-non-literal-dynamic-asset-import --json`, which reports SMITHERS5218 at 4:24 with the message `dynamic asset imports require a literal specifier and a literal `with { ... }` attribute object` — identical to the reference in code, position AND message.
